summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every sudo command (with invoking/target user and timestamp) to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and disabled sudo's syslog channel so those entries no longer land in the general system log (/var/log/secure or journal). Verified pre- and post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline: RHEL9 node1, sudo 1.9.17p2 compiled with --with-logging=syslog --with-logfac=authpriv, confirmed default sudo commands were appearing in /var/log/secure
Wrote /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging with 'Defaults !syslog', 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"', 'Defaults log_year, log_host'; validated with visudo -c
Created /var/log/sudo-commands.log with 0600 root:root perms; confirmed SELinux context var_log_t matches /var/log/secure
Ran test sudo commands and confirmed entries (with date/year, user, host, command) appear only in the new logfile and not in /var/log/secure or journalctl _COMM=sudo COMMAND= lines
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline, triggered 'shutdown -r now' on node1 in background so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed (bef0e5ec... -> 6f7b9e68...), proving an actual reboot occurred

Post-reboot: re-verified sudoers drop-in intact, visudo -c passes, prior log entries persisted, and a new sudo command was correctly logged to the dedicated file with no corresponding entry in /var/log/secure

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands recorded with user and timestamp
evidence.summary: /var/log/sudo-commands.log entries show 'date : invoking_user : HOST=... ; PWD=...; USER=target_user ; COMMAND=...' for each sudo invocation

evidence.requirement: Entries kept out of general system log
evidence.summary: Baseline showed COMMAND= lines in /var/log/secure before the change; after adding 'Defaults !syslog' and logfile, subsequent sudo runs produced no new COMMAND= entries in /var/log/secure
visudo -c validated the drop-in both before install and again after reboot; file and its 3 rule lines unchanged post-restart
Captured boot_id bef0e5ec-ce32-423b-826a-8a5a90584d3a and confirmed sudoers config + 4-line log present before reboot
'shutdown -r now' issued in background on node1; exec stream closed as expected, confirming the reboot command was accepted before disconnect

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable for two poll attempts, then came back with boot_id 6f7b9e68-80d1-4017-8c56-ca75b9b6d0d3, different from the pre-restart boot_id, and a new uptime -s start time

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required config/data
evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers drop-in still valid, prior log entries intact, and a fresh sudo command was correctly logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with no corresponding entry in /var/log/secure
